clue.text: Maybe handouts in sale felt silly

indicators.note: silly suggests the words sale felt are jumbled into a foolish new order

explanation.surface: Someone is unimpressed by the flyers pushed at a shop sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges SALE FELT. 'Maybe' marks handouts as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed sheets given out free are one common kind of handout.

clue.text: Person complaining very little having settled into boat

indicators.note: one piece settling into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
v is the abbreviation for very, written small

explanation.surface: A grumbler has finally got comfortable aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having settled into' puts V inside KETCH, after its first letter. 'very little' means very abbreviated to its small letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yiddish-derived slang for a habitual moaner or whiner, used as a noun.

clue.text: Tease pirates going about with conspirator

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them

indicators.note: one piece going about another surrounds it

parts.note: to pirate is to copy illegally, so pirates means fakes

explanation.surface: Teasing buccaneers alongside a plotter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' puts W inside FAKES. Guy Fawkes was the Gunpowder Plot conspirator of 1605, remembered on Bonfire Night in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: He was one of the plotters who tried to blow up Parliament in 1605.

clue.text: Fish spotted crossing river

indicators.note: one word crossing another lies across its middle, so it goes inside

parts.note: it spat or it spotted, both meaning light rain began to fall

explanation.surface: An angler sees a fish being carried across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts R inside SPAT. Spotted is used in the weather sense, a few drops of rain, as in 'it spat with rain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small silvery sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Discharge comes with farewell music item

parts.note: to can someone is to sack or discharge them
ta-ta is a casual British goodbye

explanation.surface: A dismissed musician leaves with a parting song.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral composition with solos and chorus, often sacred, is a piece of music.

clue.text: Everyone outside national organisation greeting result of workers' efforts

indicators.note: one piece outside another wraps around it

parts.note: everyone means all
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A whole team surrounds a national body to welcome what its staff produced.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'workers' are worker ants, not human staff; 'outside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants pile up soil to build their mound, so the heap is the product of their labour.

clue.text: Empire-builder and senior bishop meeting poet

parts.note: Alexander the Great built a vast empire
the Pope is the Bishop of Rome, the most senior bishop

explanation.surface: A conqueror and a high churchman are introduced to a writer of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century English writer of The Rape of the Lock and An Essay on Man.

clue.text: Religious woman by me with darker day developing

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters grow into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the day is getting gloomier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges BY ME and DARKER DAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: She founded Christian Science in nineteenth-century America.

clue.text: Young animal faces frigidity getting left in booth

parts.note: a cub is a young fox, bear or lion

indicators.note: one piece put in another goes inside it

parts.note: frigidity is coldness, as in ice

explanation.surface: A young creature meets a frosty reception and is shut in a small booth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faces' just means the young animal comes first; 'getting ... in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small partitioned compartment, as in an office or changing room.

clue.text: Damage behind physics unit in school

indicators.note: behind places the word for damage after the other piece

parts.note: the gram is a unit of mass
to mar is to damage

explanation.surface: Breakage occurs behind the science lab at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Grammar school is a British secondary school that selects by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a grammar school is a selective secondary school, so the word alone can mean one.

clue.text: Glorify former group making comeback

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: a word making a comeback returns, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A once-famous band reunites to be praised.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise highly or exalt.

clue.text: Gangster wants lady noted for fortune? Too bad!

parts.note: a tough is a thug or gangster
Lady Luck personifies fortune

explanation.surface: A mobster seeks a woman famous for her wealth, but gets nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fortune' looks like money; it is chance, personified as Lady Luck.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of unsympathetic dismissal, meaning that is unfortunate but unavoidable.

clue.text: Firm certain to be established outside capital's business area

indicators.note: one piece outside another wraps around it

parts.note: sure means certain
EC is the postcode of the City of London, its financial district

explanation.surface: A company is sure to be set up beyond the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container signal; the City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and fixed in place, not liable to give way.

clue.text: Clothes from M &S are new, redesigned

indicators.note: redesigned suggests the letters are reworked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A shopper notes that the garments at Marks & Spencer have a fresh look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges M, S, ARE and NEW. M&S is Marks & Spencer, a British high-street chain famous for clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments for males, as a department or category of apparel.

clue.text: Sort of gift that's left, say, with fancy packaging

indicators.note: packaging wraps one piece around another

parts.note: lacy means fancy, ornate
eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A present left behind, perhaps, comes in fancy wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packaging' is the container signal, and 'Sort of gift that's left' is a fair definition by bequest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is a gift left in a will.

clue.text: Library annexe accommodates this language

indicators.note: the words accommodate the answer, holding it within them

explanation.surface: A library extension houses books in a certain tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the Indo-Iranian or Indo-European family of tongues.

clue.text: Ale a keg spilt?

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters splash out into a new order

explanation.surface: Beer escaping from a cask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' rearranges ALE A KEG, and the whole clue describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer pouring from a split keg is an escape of liquid.

clue.text: Leave things to someone else — or maybe not, if in car!

definitions.text: Leave things to someone else — or maybe not, if in car!

parts.words: Leave things to someone else — or maybe not, if in car!
parts.note: the idiom for stepping aside from control, which a car passenger might do literally while not leaving anything to anyone

explanation.surface: Advice to delegate, with a joke about seating in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means letting others lead; in a car you could do it physically, sitting in the rear, so the literal reading undercuts the idiomatic one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to accept a less prominent role and let others take charge.

clue.text: Six men entertaining model who likes being welcomed?

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest within

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
to sit is to model or pose for an artist

explanation.surface: Six men host a fashion model who enjoys a warm reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' is the container signal: the six men host the model as a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest or caller hopes to be received warmly.

clue.text: Blunder, the thing evident in Conservative realm?

indicators.note: something evident in another is seen within it

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
to err is to blunder
it means the thing

explanation.surface: A political gaffe is apparent across the Tory domain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evident in' is the container signal; the question mark covers the joke of a Tory realm.
explanation.definitionFit: An area under a ruler's control, a domain.

clue.text: Workshop with house provided for a person putting others up

indicators.note: one piece provided for the letter a stands in its place

parts.note: an atelier is an artist's workshop or studio

explanation.surface: A workshop comes with a home for someone who lifts others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided for a' swaps the A of ATELIER for HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs an inn or guesthouse gives guests lodging.

clue.text: Sad guard, a gent travelling the normal distance for railways

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: A melancholy railway guard and a gentleman are on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges SAD GUARD A GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual spacing between rails, four feet eight and a half inches.

clue.text: Arts graduate's succeeded in word puzzle with lots of twists and turns

definitions.text: with lots of twists and turns

indicators.note: succeeded marks the abbreviation S, which the graduate replaces in the puzzle

parts.note: an acrostic is a word puzzle using initial letters
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is an arts graduate

explanation.surface: A humanities graduate has triumphed at a word game full of twists.
explanation.walkthrough: BA takes the place of S, short for succeeded, in ACROSTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnastic and agile, full of tumbling feats.

clue.text: Money for kisses?

definitions.meaning: a smacker is a loud kiss, so the plural means kisses

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for currency units, and also for loud smacking kisses.

clue.text: Shield that gives way under pressure?

definitions.meaning: a small round shield held by a handle
one who buckles collapses under strain

explanation.definitionFit: A small round shield, and whimsically one that buckles or collapses.

clue.text: Sergeant Major, hard character, lifting weights

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the letters, so they read upwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a card is an eccentric character

explanation.surface: A tough sergeant major hoists dumb-bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' reverses SMHCARD, the whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: Drachms are old apothecaries' units of weight.

clue.text: Dealer unable to pay debts ending in stir

parts.note: broke means penniless

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of stir

explanation.surface: A trader who goes bankrupt ends up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' looks like slang for prison; only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockbroker or agent who buys and sells for others.

clue.text: Doctor has to employ electronic device

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
to use is to employ

explanation.surface: A doctor needs to use a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer pointing device is an electronic peripheral.
